thread:
jules: Did a quick audit on the new toolbar strip in the Console. Noticed several accessibility regressions after the layout change across small screens: 1) focus order jumps (search -> avatar -> last used model) instead of logical left-to-right. 2) the mute/unmute icon buttons announce only \"button\" in VoiceOver. 3) contrast for the secondary ghost buttons doesn't hit 4.5:1 on dark theme. Screenshot: https://redwood.dev/snip/console-toolbar-a11y.png

harper: Thanks for the flag. Can you repro steps and the exact SR output?

jules: Steps: Tab through from the leftmost toolbar item on macOS+VoiceOver: focus lands on Search (ok), then skips to Account avatar, then goes backward to Model selector. VoiceOver reads for the mute icon: \"button\" (no label). ChromeVox on Linux shows similar. Expected: each control should have a short accessible name like 'Mute notifications' / 'Unmute notifications', and focus order should follow DOM order (left-to-right).

rory: Sounds like we might have moved interactive elements out of DOM order for layout reasons (flex reordering). If we used CSS order we need to ensure DOM order matches. Prefer keeping DOM order and using CSS to position visually OR make explicit tabindex=0/ tabindex=-1 adjustments carefully.

jules: Correct. Also the model dropdown uses aria-haspopup but no aria-expanded toggle, so SR users can't tell if it's open.

harper: Proposed short fixes: - Reflow DOM so order is logical (Search, Model selector, Run, Notifications, Avatar). - Add aria-labels to icon-only buttons, e.g., `<button aria-label=\"Mute notifications\">` - Ensure dropdowns manage `aria-expanded` and move focus into the popup on open.

dina: On contrast: dark theme ghost button #BFC7CF on #0B1220 = 3.6:1. Suggest #D2D8DF or add a 1px border with a darker stroke to reach 4.5:1 while keeping visual weight low. aria-bot ran a scan: `aria-bot: toolbar-contrast: notifications-button fail 3.6:1; avatar-button ok; icon-button missing name`.

rory: For keyboard semantics: the Run button has a split action: primary click kicks a run, secondary caret opens a menu. Currently both controls are masked into one element with JS handling Space vs Enter differently. That's bad for SR users. We should expose two controls: `<button class=\"run-primary\">Run</button><button aria-label=\"Run options\" class=\"run-menu\">▾</button>` so SR users can choose.

harper: Yes — split buttons are the accessible approach. If we must keep a single composite control, we need `aria-haspopup=\"menu\"` on the trigger and ensure the menu is focusable and announced. But split is simpler.

jules: Also saw focus outline removed globally (`:focus { outline: none; }`) — please don't strip outlines. Use `:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none; }` and a clear focus-visible style. Example CSS suggested:
```css
.toolbar-button:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid rgba(255, 194, 10, 0.18);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  border-radius: 6px;
}
```
Works for keyboard users and keeps mouse unobtrusive.

dina: Small copy nits: change 'Run' tooltip to 'Run this model' so SR announces context when the button is focused in an environment with multiple run buttons. Keep tooltip text concise.

harper: On ARIA for the dropdown: ensure the menu uses `role=\"menu\"` and items `role=\"menuitem\"` or use a listbox if it behaves like selection. Also add roving tabindex so only the focused item is tabbable.

rory: Implementation tasks: 1) re-order DOM to logical sequence, 2) add explicit aria-labels for all icon-only buttons, 3) split run button into primary + menu, 4) ensure dropdowns set aria-expanded and move focus, 5) update CSS for focus-visible and revisit global outline resets, 6) tweak dark theme contrast. I'll send a PR.

aria-bot: automated-scan: found 5 issues: missing accessible name on 2 icon buttons, contrast failures on 3 elements, missing aria-expanded on 1 dropdown, focus-order mismatch on flex-ordered toolbar.

jules: For testing: can someone verify NVDA+Firefox on Windows for the split-run behavior and VoiceOver for aria-expanded announcements? I'll add acceptance criteria: keyboard order matches visual order, SR reads descriptive names, no outline removed for keyboard, contrast >=4.5:1.

dina: I'll test dark theme contrast and run the axe+pa11y checks. Harper, please include small unit tests asserting `aria-label` presence for icon buttons; a snapshot test should catch regressions.

harper: Will do. PR title: "toolbar: accessibility fixes (DOM order, aria labels, split-run, focus-visible, contrast)". Linking this thread. Thanks y'all — small change set but should fix the most visible SR/keyboard regressions.

rory: One more tiny UX note: for screen reader verbosity, prefer short labels and keep status-only badges visually augmented with `aria-hidden=\"true\"` and separate sr-only text for the status (to avoid redundant reads when the pill is updated).

jules: Agreed. Thanks team. I'll follow up after the QA sweep.
